verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 Orion capsule has 330 cubic feet (about 9.3 cubic meters) of habitable volume.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion’s cabin has a habitable volume of 330 cubic feet'; R2: 'The cabin of Orion is comprised of 330 habitable cubic feet'; R3: 'only has about 330 cubic feet of habitable space'; R5: 'interior space of 330 cubic feet'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state 330 cubic feet habitable volume; 9.3 m³ is accurate conversion.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule has a crew capacity of 4 astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'four astronauts will fly inside the Orion spacecraft'; R2: 'four astronauts on the Artemis II mission, onboard Orion'; R3: 'fly four crewmembers'; R4: 'Crew size 4'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four-astronaut crew for Orion on Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule offers 60% more room than Apollo command modules.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion has nearly 60 percent more space than the Apollo command module’s 210 cubic feet'; R2: 'Orion has nearly 60% more space than the Apollo command module’s 210 cubic feet'; R5: 'nearly 60% larger than its Apollo command module predecessor'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements match 'nearly 60% more space/room' compared to Apollo command module.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is roughly 60% larger than Apollo capsules.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'nearly 60 percent more space than the Apollo command module’s 210 cubic feet'; R3: 'about 50% larger than the 210 cubic-foot command modules'; R5: 'nearly 60% larger'
verifications.reasoning: Primary NASA sources state nearly 60%; R3 approximates 50% but calculation (330/210≈57%) supports roughly 60%; no direct contradiction.
